name: Alpsee
kurzbeschreibung: Berwang, situated at an altitude of 1,336 m, charms visitors as the highest municipality in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena with alpine waters, mountain meadows, and the Bärenbad.
beschreibung:
Overview

The municipality of Berwang in the Tyrolean Außerfern region sits on a sunny high saddle at 1,336 metres above sea level, making it the highest village in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena. Framed by the towering peaks of the Lechtal Alps and commanding direct views of the Wetterstein range and the Zugspitze, the village serves as an idyllic retreat for nature lovers and hiking enthusiasts. While the famous historical Alpsee lake is geographically situated a few kilometres to the north in the Bavarian Alpine Foreland near Füssen and the royal castles, the Berwang valley enchants visitors with its own pristine mountain waters, such as the Rotlechstausee reservoir, the rushing Seebach stream, and the region's highest forest swimming pool.

Natural Spaces & Mountain Waters

The Berwang high plateau is criss-crossed by crystal-clear alpine brooks, blooming mountain meadows, and shaded alpine woodlands. A popular hiking excursion leads from Berwang into the hamlet of Rinnen and onwards to the idyllically situated Rotlechstausee reservoir, whose emerald-green waters are enclosed by steep rock faces and coniferous forests. A scenic circular hiking path encircles the reservoir and leads further to the thundering Rotlech waterfall. For refreshing aquatic fun right in Berwang, head to the historic Bärenbad Berwang (Bärenarena) – a heated open-air forest swimming pool situated at over 1,300 metres above sea level with spacious sunbathing lawns, a children's pool, and panoramic vistas of the surrounding Berwang mountains. Travellers seeking larger natural alpine lakes can easily reach the Heiterwanger See, Plansee, or the deep blue Blindsee on the Fernpass within a short drive.

Visiting & Getting There

The mountains and hiking trails around Berwang are freely accessible year-round without admission charges; the main hiking season spans from May to October, while winter transforms the valley into a family-friendly ski resort. The Bärenbad Berwang outdoor pool opens during the summer months (approximately mid-June to early September) on days with suitable swimming weather from 09:30 to 19:00. By car: from the north toll-free via Garmisch-Partenkirchen or Füssen/Reutte along the B179 (Fernpassstraße) to Bichlbach, then turn onto the L21 (Berwanger Landesstraße) and climb for about 5 minutes to Berwang. From the south via the Inntal motorway A12, take exit Imst, then follow the Fernpass (B179) to Bichlbach. By public transport: take the Außerfernbahn railway (DB/ÖBB) to the Bichlbach-Berwang train station, and connect from there with regional VVT bus line 152 directly into Berwang village centre.

Tips

The walking trail circling the Berwanger Moos wetland and the panorama promenade are paved or surfaced with fine gravel, making them ideal for prams, pushchairs, and barrier-free walks. For a relaxing culinary stop, traditional mountain huts around Berwang, such as the Hochthörle-Hütte or Jägerhaus-Hütte, come highly recommended. On warm summer days, be sure to pack swimwear for the Bärenbad or a picnic blanket to relax on the alpine pastures beside the Seebach stream.
